title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and operational processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, contractors, and partners who need to understand governance, approval workflows, and where to find templates and forms. Owners and points of contact are listed per section.

== Owner and scope ==
- Owner: People Ops (policy maintenance)
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (technical controls)
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal (procurement, expenses, vendor contracting)
- Applies to: all Redwood personnel (employees, contractors, vendors with network or data access)

## 1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable permission changes.

Access tiers:
- Tier 1 — Basic employee access: email, SSO, internal docs, basic tooling.
- Tier 2 — Elevated access: service accounts, CI/CD, non-prod infra. Requires manager + team lead approval.
- Tier 3 — Sensitive access: production infra, customer data, KMS/HSM. Requires manager + security review + documented business justification.

Key controls and processes:
1. Provisioning:
   - New hires and contractors must submit an access request via the People Ops portal within 3 business days of start date.
   - Manager submits requested role(s) and justifications. Default access bundles for common roles exist in the Access Catalog.
2. Approval flow:
   - Manager approval → Team owner review → Security review for Tier 3. Automated SSO group assignment on approval.
3. Periodic reviews:
   - Monthly automated access report for critical resources (production clusters, secrets stores).
   - Quarterly company-wide access certification; managers attest for direct reports.
4. Offboarding:
   - Offboarding checklist (People Ops) triggers deprovisioning: SSO disabled same day, laptop recovery, service account rotation for owned keys.
5. Emergency access (break-glass):
   - Time-limited emergency role issued via the incident runbook. Requires post-hoc audit entry and manager justification within 48 hours.

Required documentation and artifacts:
- Access request form link: [People Ops Portal] (internal)
- Access Catalog (documented role bundles)
- Audit logs retained for 2 years for privileged changes

## 2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce operational risk by standardizing how infrastructure and production changes are proposed, reviewed, and executed.

Change categories:
- Standard change: Low risk, pre-approved routine tasks (config tweaks, scheduled deploys under thresholds).
- Normal change: Requires change ticket, risk assessment, scheduling, and rollback plan.
- Emergency change: Applied to mitigate an ongoing outage or security incident; documented after the fact and reviewed by the CAB.

Procedures:
1. Submit change request in the Change Board system with: description, owner, rollback plan, impact window, stakeholders, and verification steps.
2. Risk assessment: Low/Medium/High scoring based on service criticality and blast radius.
3. Approval:
   - Low risk: Team lead approval.
   - Medium risk: Engineering manager + SRE approval.
   - High risk: Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval and scheduled maintenance window.
4. Execution: Follow runbook steps, take pre-change snapshot/backups, notify stakeholders.
5. Post-change verification and summary posted to change ticket.

Emergency change process:
- Notify on-call, perform immediate mitigation, and open a postmortem if the change occurred during an incident. CAB review within 5 business days.

Change windows and maintenance calendar:
- Non-critical changes schedule Monday–Friday 00:00–06:00 UTC by default.
- High-impact changes require at least 72 hours lead time and communication to affected customers and internal teams.

## 3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect company and customer data through classification, retention, and handling rules.

Data classification levels:
- Public — safe for public distribution.
- Internal — company use only; no customer sensitive data.
- Confidential — contains business-sensitive information (financials, roadmaps).
- Restricted — customer PII/regulated data or secrets. Access limited and logged.

Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Access: Restricted data requires Tier 3 access processes and data processing agreements for vendors.
- Masking/Pseudonymization: For analytics, transform Restricted data before use in non-secure environments.

Retention & deletion:
| Data type | Classification | Retention period | Responsible owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Logs (standard) | Internal | 180 days | Eng-SRE |
| Audit logs (privileged) | Restricted | 2 years | Security & Compliance |
| Customer datasets | Restricted | Per contract; default 7 years | Product/Legal |

Backups and DR:
- Backups taken daily for critical stateful services, weekly for lower-tier data. Verify restores quarterly.
- DR RTO/RPO defined per service in the runbook and monitored via post-DR test reports.

Data sharing and external transfers:
- All transfers of Restricted data to third parties require a Data Protection Addendum and approval from Security & Legal.

## 4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing behavior, improve cost control, and ensure compliance with contracting rules.

Approval matrix (examples):
- < $1,000 — Requestor’s manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000 — Manager + Finance approval.
- > $25,000 — Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor (Procurement team coordinates).

Procurement process:
1. Complete a Purchase Request (PR) form with justification, budget code, and vendor details.
2. Obtain required approvals per approval matrix.
3. Procurement team issues PO and sends to vendor. No commitment > $25k without signed contract.
4. For recurring SaaS, procurement/Finance evaluates security questionnaire and SSO/SCIM support.

Corporate card & expense policy:
- Cardholders must submit receipts within 7 days of purchase.
- Acceptable expenses: travel, meeting food (team budget thresholds), approved software, minor office supplies.
- Prohibited: cash advances, personal items, fines/penalties.
- Expense submission: use Expense tool; tagged with project code and receipt attached. Audits occur quarterly.

Reimbursement timeline:
- Standard reimbursement: 30 days after submission and approval.

## 5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Manage third-party risk, ensure contractual protections, and maintain an updated vendor inventory.

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Identification & intake: Requestor completes Vendor Intake form with scope and data access requirements.
2. Due diligence: Security questionnaire (high-risk vendors require a SOC2/ISO report), legal review of contract, privacy review for data processors.
3. Onboarding: Create vendor record in Vendor Registry, assign owner, configure least-privilege access.
4. Ongoing monitoring: Annual security re-assessment for critical vendors; contract renewal reviews 90 days prior to expiry.
5. Offboarding: Revoke access, confirm data return/destruction per contract.

High-risk vendor controls:
- Additional contractual clauses: breach notification within 72 hours, right to audit, encryption requirements, subcontractor disclosure.
- Technical controls: SSO integration, IP allowlists, limited data retention window.

## 6) Travel Policies
Purpose: Keep travel safe and cost-effective while minimizing administrative burden.

Booking and approvals:
- All business travel must be pre-approved in the Travel tool by the employee’s manager.
- Preferred vendors (airlines, hotels, car rental) are listed in the Travel Portal. Book through the portal for policy-compliant rates.

Per diem and allowed expenses:
- Meals: capped per city band (see Travel Portal table). Receipts required for single items > $25.
- Lodging: Use corporate rate where available.
- Transportation: Economy class for flights under 6 hours; business class only with Exec approval for flights > 6 hours.

Safety & incident reporting:
- Report travel incidents to People Ops and Security immediately. For emergencies, Security provides local assistance and evacuation coordination.

Expense submission:
- Submit within 14 days of trip completion with itemized receipts. Delays may be denied.

## 7) Internal Templates and Naming Conventions
Available templates (People Ops / Finance / Eng):
- Offer letter, NDAs, contractor SOW template (People Ops)
- Vendor Intake form, PO template, Contract redline checklist (Finance & Legal)
- Incident runbook template, Change request template, Runbook verification checklist (Eng-SRE)
- Meeting notes and decision record (ADR) template (Engineering)

Document naming conventions:
- Use hyphen-delimited lower case: team-document-type-YYYYMMDD (e.g., eng-sre-incident-postmortem-20260701)
- Add status suffix when a draft: -draft, and -final when published.

Storage and retention:
- Authoritative policies live in Confluence under the policies-and-process space.
- Templates stored in the Templates library with version history.

== How to provide feedback or request exceptions ==
- File a Policy Exception request in the Policy Exceptions tracker. Exceptions require a documented business justification, compensating controls, and sign-off by the policy owner and Security (duration-limited, reviewed quarterly).
